item.title: The Clock is Ticking for the Detroit Red Wing and Simon Edvinsson
item.dc:creator: Mark Easson
item.description: Simon Edvinsson needs to be signed to an NHL contract by December 1st to be eligible to play in the NHL this season. Time is running out.
item.content:encoded:
The December 1st deadline to get Simon Edvinsson signed is fast approaching

NHL Network: The Detroit Red Wings have set the price high for RFA defenseman Simon Edvinsson. The Wings have struggled of late and the playoff gap is widening. The December 1st deadline is fast approaching.

** NHLRumors.com transcription

Michael Rupp: “Yeah, no, that’s a great point. Talking about if this team continues to maybe struggle in Detroit, but there’s I don’t know. I’m looking at the standings here, and there’s we’re starting to get some separation already, which we haven’t seen in recent years. Whether that’s going to sustain and it’s going to continue to get wider, that gap.

The Minnesota Wild are All-In and Quinn Hughes Isn’t Going Anywhere

Does that help a situation with Edvinsson? Do you think, as far as we know, the deadline (December 1st) that they have to have something in place by? Do you, do you see maybe we’re getting into a spot right now where the standings are starting to open up?

Friedman: “I do think that, that could potentially play a factor. This one with Edvinsson, like it does seem to me like it’s a little bit, Mike of, like, who’s got the more nerves of steel here? Is it, you know, like I said, the Red Wings have a high bar. They have a really high bar for Edvinsson, like they do for Larkin, and nobody has hit that.

And you know, I think there’s a few things in the Edvinsson situation that play a factor in all this. Number one, there is the December 1st, and I do think there, like I said, there’s a little bit of who’s got the stronger nerves. Who bends first.

Like, you know, one of the things that you know some reporters who live in Sweden have told me is that they believe that if you know it goes past December 1st, he’s prepared to play there. Like, that’s how strong his resolve is. But you know, we’ll see. We won’t know that for another 16,17 days.

The thing about Edvinsson that’s really interesting is that, first of all, he’s almost he’s unique. There’s not too many people as big as him who are as effective as he is? There, there really is nobody to replace him for Detroit. And there’s nobody in the draft this year that you look at and say, that’s a guy you can draft who can be that player in a few years. He’s, he’s very unique.

NHL Rumors: Nothing Has Changed with Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson

You know, I’ll say this though: I did have some teams say to me they really like the player a lot, but when you look at the acquisition cost, and what you’re going to have to pay him, it’s really, really steep what Detroit is trying to do here. So, I just think it’s poker, and everybody’s at the table waiting to see who blinks first.”

item.title: NHL Rumors: Vancouver Canucks, and the Minnesota Wild
item.dc:creator: Mark Easson
item.description: It may not be easy to move some of their veteran players for the Canucks. Bill Guerin won't guarantee that he won't trade Quinn Hughes.
item.content:encoded:
Vancouver Canucks veterans may not hold much value

Halford and Brough: Rick Dhaliwal said that one contending team has zero interest in any Vancouver Canucks players, and unrestricted free agents have little interest in playing for the rebuilding Canucks.

“One team told me this week they have no interest in Vancouver players. They said we have not discussed, and it’s a really good hockey club, and they have not discussed any Canucks. So that’s a problem they face, and it points to what you just said, Jason.

And for those in the market who say, ‘Oh, trade the vets. Oh, you can get vets anywhere, anytime.’ Okay. Well, let’s diagnose that comment. Canucks got (Brendan) Gallagher, (Luke) Schenn, (Paul) Cotter, and (Jamie) Oleksiak in the summer. Right? All four have been healthy scratches.

You are not getting good veterans on July 1st to come to Vancouver, I’m sorry, in a rebuild. No, no, no. You are not on July 1st getting a stud forward. Those, most free agents on July 1st are over the age of 30 or nearing 30 and want nothing to do with the city of Vancouver and a rebuild. Vancouver is not a destination, just so you guys know, and everybody else knows, it’s not a destination.”

NHL Rumors: Anaheim Ducks, and the Calgary Flames

Only Detroit knows what Minnesota offered for Dylan Larkin, and Guerin isn’t prepared to guarantee he wouldn’t trade Quinn Hughes

Nicholas J. Cotsonika of NHL.com: Minnesota Wild GM Bill Guerin on News Talk 830 WCCO on forward Danila Yurov:

“Hey, look, I know there are reports out there that we have offered him up, but nobody knows what I’ve offered, except Detroit.”

Guerin told NHL.com on Tuesday that he’d be willing to hold on to pending UFA Quinn Hughes beyond the March 1st trade deadline. He was asked on WCCO if he’s decided to not trade Hughes by the deadline no matter what, and Guerin said:

“No. I haven’t decided that. No. I haven’t decided anything.”

When Guerin was asked if he knows when he’ll decide, he said:

“No. I don’t. When you make decisions like that, you have to stand behind them, and I’m not prepared to do anything like that right now.”

item.title: Philadelphia Flyers Trade Candidates
item.dc:creator: Mark Easson
item.description: The Philadelphia Flyers sit awfully close to the Eastern Conference basement, and they could look to move some players before the trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
If things continue to go south for the Philadelphia Flyers, they have some trade candidates to move out

Daily Faceoff: Anthony Di Marco, when asked which Philadelphia Flyers could be on the move before the March 1st NHL Trade Deadline.

Yaremchuk: “Who else are you looking at as pieces that this front office might try sell off in the next, you know, call it four or five months leading into the deadline?

Di Marco: “Well, it feels like he’s been on the trade block for three years, but Rasmus Ristolainen. I would be utterly shocked if he’s a Flyer beyond the trade deadline. Like, I mean, I think even if it’s for a second-round pick, which they could have gotten last year.

I look at a guy like Owen Tippett. I know a lot of Edmonton faithful have had their eyes on him for a while.

The Flyers Were Genuinely Shocked by the Matvei Michkov Report. Was there an Agenda?

And then you look at a Travis Konecny, who I’ve reported a few times, the Flyers would be open to approaching him to waive his no-movement clause. I think in an ideal world you would go after Travis Konecny, and I know a lot of fans hate him right now in Philadelphia, and that’s all well and good, but I’ve spoken to several teams going back to last winter that would have a ton of time for Travis Konecny.

Yes, he’s in year two of an eight-year contract at $8.75 (million). But again, with the rising salary cap, you put Travis Konecny on a second line of a Stanley Cup team. Like, let’s say the Minnesota Wild, I think that he could do a lot of damage there. The problem there is once again, is he going to waive his no-movement clause?

So I mean, I think they have a lot of pieces to overturn this. There’s a chance that the Flyers have two picks inside the top 10 this upcoming draft. So I think that you have to prepare yourselves for that possibility and just stockpile assets in the meantime.

And I really do think that the Flyers will take a hard look at taking axes to that leaders doesn’t turn around. And for me, I know the trade protection is a big block in the road, but I think Travis Konecny would be a prime candidate to really shake things up.
